candidates.review: Transfer the common-reader error fix into both selected native ext4/F2FS Merkle readers: only -ENOENT can trigger speculative readahead; other lookup errors return unchanged. Drop existing stale references before demand reading and propagate demand-read failure. Keep native offsets and the invalidate lock from 05ae9392c7c8. Avoid extra I/O on allocation/error paths without weakening hash verification. Extracted tests pass 160 cases/1520 assertions with retry-on-error and leaked-reference controls rejected.

The exported standalone signature helper was explicitly removed by 7f2bfb86500c after its incfs caller was removed. Both complete patches and current signature/header/incfs sources examined: final ACK and port lack __fsverity_verify_signature and preserve native verification instead. Do not restore the removed wrapper or its permissive disabled-signature stub. Native signature validation retains the empty-keyring parser-avoidance check and LSM integrity notification (SDK built-in signatures disabled). Incfs still implements its separately retained digest/metadata API; absence of a caller alone is not the rationale.

Native LTS contains e77000ccc531 initialization handling: SLAB_PANIC info cache, workqueue/keyring panic on failure, void initialization helpers and no unused exit paths. The full affected fs/verity files and private header are identical to pinned LTS. Later native register_sysctl_init supersedes the manual sysctl registration/panic handling. Keep native boot-failure behavior and all signature checks; do not reintroduce ACK standalone signature wrapper context.

Native LTS contains 456ae5fe9b44: sysctl setup resides in init.c and runs independently of built-in signature support; only require_signatures table entry is conditional. Later register_sysctl_init and sized const table supersede the old header/sentinel. All affected files equal LTS. The SDK disables built-in signatures but retains the common fsverity sysctl directory setup. Native access mode/bounds on require_signatures remain.

Keep native per-filesystem fsverity_cleanup_inode ownership rather than moving it into generic clear_inode. Reviewed ext4_clear_inode, F2FS post-eviction including async split, and both btrfs eviction exits: each still cleans its info exactly at the native lifecycle point. Native cleanup frees and clears the inode-owned pointer; generic clear_inode has no duplicate call. This is an internal ownership refactor, not a new Android userspace or hook operation. SDK ext4/F2FS retain verification and cleanup; btrfs is disabled. No need to change generic VFS lifetime or adopt a hash-table representation for this refactor.

Keep native inode-based write_merkle_tree_block API. Every changed filesystem callback immediately converts the proposed file argument back to the same inode; native build_merkle_tree already obtains that inode from its live filp. Ext4/F2FS metadata offsets, pagecache writes and errors are therefore retained with no new target behavior required. Btrfs callback is native and disabled in SDK. The motivating new iomap/XFS implementation is outside this target; this does not omit hash writes or verification. Vendor hooks are unaffected; this is an internal filesystem operation signature, not historical binary KMI.

Keep two native filesystem Merkle-page readers instead of moving their identical cache/read sequence into a common helper. Each retains its own metadata offset and native __filemap_get_folio behavior; SDK F2FS fault injection is disabled. Port the substantive later error-path fix 36f66dd separately in 8e1d83f93ebd and preserve shared invalidate locking. No hash operation, userspace API or vendor hook is removed by retaining the local implementation. A common helper needed by a future XFS implementation is not necessary for the configured ext4/F2FS target.
